title: Enterprise audit-response slate for security questions
content:
Purpose:
This working slate gives sales and CSEs short, tested language and specimen evidence attachments to respond to enterprise security questionnaires and audit requests focused on SOC2/ISO/HIPAA, data handling, and audit-log expectations. Draft is intentionally pragmatic — short answers + where to pull artifacts from so reps can reply within 24 hours.

Audience:
- AE/SE/CSE preparing for procurement/RFP Q&A
- Solutions engineers doing customer security walkthroughs
- Product marketing for one-pagers and slide bullets

TL;DR positioning (two lines):
- Redwood Inference operates a production-first inference platform with explicit controls for data residency, encryption, and auditability; we provide customer-scoped audit telemetry, configurable retention, and enterprise evidence packages for SOC2/ISO/HIPAA requests.
- For sensitive workloads customers can choose Dedicated or Private deployment where data plane isolation and customer-controlled KMS are standard.

Recommended short answers (copy-pasteable):
1) SOC2/ISO/HIPAA readiness:
- "Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II coverage for our hosted control plane and publishes an evidence kit on request. For regulated workloads we offer Private and Dedicated deployment options which map to additional controls (customer KMS, VPC peering, on-prem integrations)."
- Follow-up evidence to attach: SOC2 report (redwood-soc2-2025.pdf), ISO27001 scope statement (iso-scope-2025.pdf), HIPAA BA agreement template (BAA-template.pdf).

2) Data handling & residency:
- "Customers choose where inference runs: hosted regions, Dedicated pools, or Private deployments. For hosted operations, PII and content are isolated per tenant; customers may opt out of storing request/response payloads. Data residency controls include region selectors and signed Data Processing Addendum (DPA)."
- Evidence: DPA template, region availability matrix (regions-availability.csv).

3) Audit logs / telemetry:
- Short language to use in slides/emails: "We emit tenant-scoped audit logs containing request timestamp, request id, model id and variant, route name, token counts, latency metrics and user/role identity for control-plane actions. Customers can export logs via Console or our Export API; retention is configurable to meet audit requirements."
- Important clarifier: "By default we do not store full prompt/response payloads in long-term telemetry. For customers that need payload-level logging for debugging or compliance, this can be enabled explicitly and scoped to the customer’s retention policy."
- Evidence: sample audit-log export (audit-export-sample.json), Console screenshot (console-audit-page.png).

Competitor-differentiation notes (bullet points for pitches):
- Versus general cloud AI endpoints: Redwood provides a pre-packaged, audit-ready evidence kit and controls tuned for inference (KV cache controls, model variant pinning) rather than DIY endpoint glue.
- Versus single-tenant inference vendors: We balance dedicated isolation with managed operations and faster GTM than full on-prem projects.
- Versus turnkey hosted LLM APIs: we offer explicit fallbacks and routing policies to control cost + reliability that are often missing from commodity APIs — this matters to SRE/infra teams evaluating audit and disaster recovery controls.

Common procurement questions + recommended answers (short, then pointer):
Q: "Can you include prompt contents in logs?"
A: "Yes — only if the customer enables payload logging. This is disabled by default for privacy-sensitive customers. For Private/Dedicated deployments we support customer-managed log sinks." -> Attach: logging-config-guide.md

Q: "What is your key management posture?"
A: "Platform encrypts data at rest and in transit. For Private/Dedicated customers we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM) so keys can be customer-controlled." -> Attach: kms-integration-notes.pdf

Q: "What does your incident response and RCA pipeline look like?"
A: "We operate a documented IR process with 24/7 on-call engineering. We provide incident timelines and post-mortems for customer-impacting events as part of enterprise SLAs. SOC2 report includes controls for incident detection and response." -> Attach: IR-runbook-summary.pdf

Evidence checklist by ask type (quick pick):
- Basic security ask: SOC2 report, Network diagram, Access control matrix snapshot
- HIPAA / regulated data: BAA template, encryption proof, KMS integration notes, Private deployment architecture
- Deep telemetry/audit: sample audit-log export, retention configurations, export API spec
- Pen test and vuln mgmt: latest pen test exec summary, SCA report, CVE tracking policy

Specimen audit-log disclosure language (short + long variants):
- Short: "Redwood provides tenant-scoped audit logs with request metadata and control-plane events; payload logging is opt-in."
- Long: "Redwood’s audit logs include per-request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model_id, route, token usage, latency), control-plane user and role events (login, key rotation, permission changes), and system health telemetry. Customers may enable full payload capture for their tenant; retained payloads are subject to customer-configured retention and deletion policies. Logs can be exported through the Console or via the Audit Export API in NDJSON/CSV formats for ingestion into SIEMs."

Sample email response template for a security buyer (short):
Hi <Name>,
Thanks — attached is our SOC2 Type II cover letter and an audit-log sample. Short answers below and we can jump on a call to walk through architecture and export APIs.
- SOC2/ISO: attached (redwood-soc2-2025.pdf, iso-scope-2025.pdf)
- Audit logs: tenant-scoped metadata exported via Console/API; payload logging is opt-in (audit-export-sample.json attached)
- Data residency: region controls + DPA available
Please let me know a good time to run through this with our security engineer — we can produce a tailored evidence package for your procurement team.
Thanks,
<AE name>

Operational notes for CSEs (actionable):
- Quick pulls: SOC2 and ISO artifacts live in /evidence/g2m/2025/ in the shared Confluence repo. Use the template email to reply within 24 hours.
- If customer requests prompt/response payload retention be enabled, open a ticket to infra with tag "audit-payload-enable" and set expected retention in the ticket (we must log rationale and owner for compliance).
- For Private deployment asks route to sales-engineering: include architecture diagram + KMS/peering checklist.

Open questions to resolve (internal):
- Standardize a single naming convention for audit exports (currently three ad-hoc filenames exist). Owner: Jonah Park.
- Decide canonical retention ranges we will pre-quote (30/90/365 days) and pricing implications. Owner: Priya Nair.
- Finalize SOC2 artifact redaction rules for sharing (PII redaction checklist). Owner: Ethan Rivera.

Next steps (this doc is a living slate):
1) GTM to adopt short answers above into the sales playbook and email templates (owner: Maya Chen)
2) Security to drop canonical artifact paths into evidence repo and confirm shareable files (owner: Ethan Rivera)
3) Engineering to create a single, documented audit-export filename and add sample export to evidence bucket (owner: Jonah Park)

Notes / Tone guidance for reps:
- Keep answers simple and factual; default to "we can provide X artifact" rather than long technical prose.
- If a question goes deeper than the canned response, offer a call and loop in a security engineer — don’t guess.
- Emphasize deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) as levers customers can use to meet regulatory constraints.

Appendix — short artifact index (where to pull files):
- redwood-soc2-2025.pdf (Confluence/GDrive: /evidence/SOC2/)
- iso-scope-2025.pdf (Confluence: /evidence/ISO/)
- BAA-template.pdf (Confluence: /legal/BAA/)
- audit-export-sample.json (Shared bucket: /evidence/audit_samples/)
- kms-integration-notes.pdf (Confluence: /security/kms/)

This doc is intentionally terse. For walkthroughs and custom evidence bundles, route requests to gtm-compliance@redwood.ai or book time with the security evidence team via the Confluence booking grid.

-- End of working slate --
